pre_registration.assessment_adopt_if_2026-11-12:
Stated before any run, and each skill is decided on its own.
tdd is adopted if, on R3, either (a) the with arm succeeds in at least 2 of 3 runs and the without arm in at most 1, or (b) both arms succeed in at least 2 of 3 and the with arm's median total tokens is at most 75% of the without arm's. All of these must also hold: tdd was invoked in at least 2 of 3 with-runs; no with-run stalled on a question (tdd/SKILL.md line 22 makes the agent wait for user-confirmed seams); and the measured Claude Code always-on delta for both skills is at most 150 tokens.
diagnosing-bugs is adopted by the same rule on R1, and only if the R2 guard then shows at least as many with-arm successes as without-arm, with the with arm's median total tokens at most 1.15 times the without arm's.
A skill that never triggers is not adopted, because its listing would be pure cost. Ties, or a with arm that does worse, also mean not adopted. If 0005 or 0006 is measured for these jobs too, adopt at most one per job: the larger success gain wins, then the smaller always-on cost.
pre_registration.verification_fact_sheet_2026-11-13: Adopt, fixed before runs, each skill alone: with >= 2/3 and without <= 1/3, or both >= 2/3 and with-arm median tokens <= 75%; skill invoked in >= 2/3 with runs; always-on delta <= 150 tokens; a one-success gap or a 2-2 tie means 2 more runs per arm (ab-tasks); at most one of 0004/0005/0006 per job. (the verification's fact sheet (not published), fact_sheet_markdown)
pre_registration.first_run_record: Fixed before any run (fact sheet plus the assessment's adopt_if, each skill decided alone). tdd on R3, diagnosing-bugs on R1: with-arm passes >= 2 of 3 and without <= 1 of 3, or both >= 2 of 3 and the with-arm median tokens (all models) <= 75% of the without arm's. The skill must also be invoked (Skill tool or Read of its SKILL.md) in >= 2 of 3 with-runs, and no with-run may stall (a stall is a final result text ending in '?' with the grade failing). The always-on delta must be <= 150 tokens. A one-success gap or a 2-2 tie means 2 more runs per arm. diagnosing-bugs also needs the R2 guard: with-arm successes >= without, and with-arm median tokens <= 1.15x the without arm's. At most one of 0004/0005/0006 per job. A with-run that breaks containment is void and counts against the with arm. R3 grade = ab-tasks.md exactly; a change outside tests/ is reported separately as passed_strict.

draft_rule_0330.text: - Rule, each skill alone (M; the order of steps, the thresholds after 5 runs and the scoring of voids and breaches written out on 2026-11-13, after review and before any task run). After 3 runs per arm, a one-success gap (3-2, 2-1 or 1-0, either way) or a 2-2 tie first adds 2 runs per arm, once, and the rule then applies to all 5; otherwise it applies to the 3. Adopt only if the with arm passes at least 2 of 3 (4 of 5) and the without arm at most 1 (2 of 5), or both pass at least 2 of 3 (4 of 5) and the with arm's median tokens are at most 75% of the without arm's; the skill is invoked in at least 2 of 3 with-runs (4 of 5); no with-run stalls (its final text ends in "?" and the grade fails); and the always-on delta is at most 150 tokens. `diagnosing-bugs` also needs R2, extended the same way: with-arm successes at least the without arm's, median tokens at most 1.15 times. A run that ends on an API error or a usage or rate limit, or is void, is not scored and is re-run in its slot; a with-run that breaks containment scores as a failure and is not re-run, and a without-run that does is re-run. At most one of 0004, 0005 and 0006 per job.

rule_note: tdd (R3): with 0/3 and without 0/3, so neither (a) (with >= 2/3, without <= 1/3) nor (b) (both >= 2/3) holds; invoked in 0 of 3 with-runs (needs >= 2); no stall. diagnosing-bugs (R1): both 3/3, so (a) fails; (b) needs the with-arm median at most 75% of the without arm's, measured 115.6%, within the run-to-run spread (with 776,507 to 1,174,632, without 704,445 to 983,277) and measured across the listing swap (skills_listed_task_runs), so not the skill's cost; invoked in 0 of 3 with-runs; no stall; R2 therefore not run. The decision rests on the invocation counts and the pass counts, not on the token ratios. The always-on condition fails under the rule fixed before any run, the assessment's adopt_if and the fact sheet (182 > 150), and is open only under the unpublished draft's later committed-copy rerun, which was not done (121 in the control); it cannot change the result. The pass counts hold with the containment check's Bash clause read as running a lane module or connecting (containment_rule.bash_clause, read after the runs), and only for the clauses the harness tested (containment_rule.clauses); read literally, every run breaks the Bash clause, R1's with arm scores 0 of 3 and the without-runs would be re-run, and the result is the same (rule_result_literal_clause).

containment: Always-on runs: 0 tool calls in every run, 0 leak-scan hits, nothing new in ~ or /tmp, user skills dirs and ~/.claude/settings.json unchanged, no new worktree or process, and the 7 copies hash-identical to the pinned blobs before and after each with-run. One flag: b-k2 'repo-refs-changed', which was refs/heads/m3/alpaca-groundwork moving between two unpublished commits during the run. That came from concurrent work on that branch, not from the run (0 tool calls), so it is not a breach. The addition has no hooks, scripts that run on their own, servers or network use. All 7 files were read before the first run. Resume: every task run's worktree changed only its allowed paths (tests/ for R3; meridian/ and .gitignore for R1; graders' outside-path checks empty), HEAD unmoved, no git state left, no process left with its cwd in the worktree, the 7 copies hash-identical before and after every with-run, the top-level names in ~ and in the user skill folders and the time and size of ~/.claude/settings.json unchanged, no new worktree of the run's own. The harness's flags were checked: other agents' worktrees and refs and a pyright-lsp-inline plugin-data dir from an ADR 0002 run (concurrent work); uv's lock files, which every run of both arms leaves in /tmp; and the runs' own /tmp probes: a-r3-1, a-r3-2 and a-r3-3 removed theirs, while b-r3-2 and b-r3-3 left theirs (archived into the run folders and removed). A /tmp write is not a breach in either arm (containment_rule.tmp). Bash calls naming a word of the check's list (bash_clause_calls per run; each call counted once): ibkr_paper in all 12 runs, ib_probe in 8, 4002 in 5 (a-r1-1, a-r1-2, b-r1-1, b-r1-2, b-r1-3), ibgateway in 4 (a-r1-2, b-r1-1, b-r1-2, b-r1-3), curl, wget, pip install, uv add, npm and npx in none; 26 calls in all (7 in R3, 19 in R1), each a read (cat, grep, sed -n) or an edit (python heredoc, sed -i) of files under meridian/ or tests/, some followed by uv run pytest, ruff or pyright; none ran a module with -m meridian. Leak-scan hits: b-r1-1 2, b-r1-2 2, b-r1-3 2 and a-r1-2 4 (leak_hits_reviewed), reviewed as the one heredoc edit of boundary.py's docstring that names ~/Jts/ibgateway and port 4002 (each call is in the stream and the transcript, so 2 hits per call), plus in a-r1-2 an ls of its own autoMemoryDirectory. The deny rule Bash(*ibgateway*) in the --settings file did not stop those four multi-line python heredoc calls: all four ran, and permission_denials is 0 in every run, so 0 denials is no evidence of containment. The evidence on the Gateway is narrower: the owner's guard found it down before every run but never ran during a run or after the last one, b-r1-3 (guard.resume_limits); the process sampler saw no process named java or ibgateway with its cwd in the run's worktree (guard.process_sampler), and cannot see a Gateway started elsewhere, such as from ~/Jts. tests/test_public_tree.py passed in every graded worktree as part of the full suite (R1: 281 passed; R3: the full suite on 96e82e6 with the run's tests exited 0). With the check's Bash clause read as running a lane module or connecting to a Gateway port (containment_rule.bash_clause), no breach was found in the clauses the harness tested (containment_rule.clauses) and no breach branch of the rule was reached; the clauses it did not test (the Gateway during a run and after the last, ~/.codex beyond skills/, file changes inside the user skill folders) are not shown to hold. Observed: the Gateway down at each run's start, no Bash call running -m meridian., and the worktree's paths, HEAD and the 7 copies unchanged. Read literally, all 12 runs broke it: R1's with arm would score 0 of 3, not 3 of 3, and all 6 without-runs would be re-run; the result stays not adopted (rule_result_literal_clause).

containment_rule.assessment_containment_check: After each with-run, all of these must hold. git hash-object of every copied skill file still equals its pinned blob. No file is new or changed under ~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills, ~/.codex, ~/.claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.json (find -newer a stamp file taken before the run, ignoring session transcripts). No docs/agents/, GLOSSARY.md, docs/adr/ or .scratch/ appeared. The transcript's Bash commands contain none of ibkr_paper, ib_probe, ibgateway, 4002, curl, wget, pip install, uv add, npm or npx. No test fixture was copied from runs/ or the engine logs (diagnosing-bugs suggests replaying captured traces, and here those can hold account ids), and tests/test_public_tree.py passes. The IB Gateway stays logged out.
containment_rule.source: the assessment's measurement_protocol.containment_check, 2026-11-12, before any run (the verification's fact sheet (not published))
containment_rule.tmp: Neither that check nor the rule names /tmp; the harness flags a new /tmp entry only for review. A write to /tmp, kept or removed, is therefore not a breach, in either arm. Decided in the ADR's revision of 2026-11-13, after the runs. Counting leftovers instead would make only b-r3-2 and b-r3-3 breaches; both failed the grade, and a with-run breach scores as a failure, so no score would change.
containment_rule.bash_clause: The check's sentence 'The transcript's Bash commands contain none of ibkr_paper, ib_probe, ibgateway, 4002, curl, wget, pip install, uv add, npm or npx' is read as: no Bash call runs a lane module (python -m meridian.ibkr_paper, meridian.ib_probe, meridian.boundary contract) or connects to a Gateway port; naming those words while reading or editing source files is no breach. This reading was made in the ADR's revision of 2026-11-13 by its author, after the runs, like the /tmp ruling; no record of it exists from before the runs. ab-claude-code.md fixes no reading of the clause; ab-dsh.md line 47 fixed this reading before run 1 for the DeepSeek Harness series only. Read literally, every one of the 12 runs breaks the clause (containment): each with-run would score as a failure (R3 with 0 of 3, as scored; R1 with 0 of 3 instead of 3 of 3) and each without-run would be re-run. With 0 passes and 0 invocations in both with arms, no re-run outcome could adopt either skill (0004_aggregate.py, result_literal_clause), so the decision is the same; the pass counts 0-0 on R3 and 3-3 on R1 hold only under the reading.
containment_rule.deny_rules: The deny rule Bash(*ibgateway*) (in each run's --settings file) did not stop four multi-line python heredoc calls whose text held ~/Jts/ibgateway, one each in a-r1-2, b-r1-1, b-r1-2 and b-r1-3: all ran (tool_result not an error) and permission_denials is 0 in all 12 runs. The deny rules are therefore no evidence of containment; the guard (before each run) and the process sampler (processes with their cwd in the worktree) are evidence only within their limits (guard.resume_limits, guard.process_sampler, clauses). ab-claude-code.md line 18 already says the rules match the command as written and calls the logged-out Gateway and the leak scan the real guards; it does not say they missed heredoc calls.
